chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever performs Tamattu' in the months of Hajj, then stays in Mecca until Hajj arrives, upon him is a sheep; and whoever performs Tamattu' in other than the months of Hajj, then resides in Mecca until Hajj arrives, there is no dam (blood sacrifice) upon him. It is a single Hajj, and the Udhiyah (sacrifice) is upon the people of the cities (Ahl al-AmSar).'

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and the first ten days of Muharram)
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْأَمْصَارِ: People of the cities (residents of Mecca)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood sacrifice (general term for animal sacrifice in Hajj context)
key_terms.شَاةٌ: A sheep (a specific type of sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sacrifice for Tamattu' Hajj depending on the time of year?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify the distinction between the sacrificial animal (dam) required for Tamattu' Hajj based on the timing of the ihram relative to the Hajj months. The hadith specifies that those who perform Tamattu' during the Hajj months and reside in Mecca must offer a sheep, whereas those who do so outside these months are exempt from the dam, treating their pilgrimage as a simple Hajj. This highlights the scholarly view that the obligation of the sacrifice is primarily incumbent upon the residents of Mecca (Ahl al-AmSar) rather than pilgrims from other regions.
